rationale: Evidence from iteration 3 (score 418, down from 443). The oval still finishes 16/20 at 1.89 s with max_error 0.045 m, so the baseline steering works on gentle curves. The s-bend fell to 2/20 finishes, and the slalom got worse: progress 0.16 (from 0.33), 0/20 finishes, and max_error about 0.063 m, which is just above the fixed 0.06 m off-track limit. The body width cannot raise that limit (0.0125 + body_width/4 stays under 0.06 for every allowed body), so tracking error on sharp alternating bends must fall. Iteration 3 changed three things at once (slower speed, wider 0.02 m sensor spacing over +/-0.06 m, kp 2.6). Slalom progress fell, so the wider spacing and higher kp are the likely causes, not speed. Hypothesis H5: the robot reacts too late to alternating bends. Sensors at y = 0.04 m see the line only after the wheels have already moved onto it, so the correction arrives late and overshoots. Changes: (1) revert to the iteration 2 sensor layout (seven sensors, 15 mm spacing, x = -0.045 to +0.045, weights [-2,-1.33,-0.67,0,0.67,1.33,2]), which had the best score and the most slalom progress; (2) move the sensors forward to y = 0.06 m to give about 2 cm more lead; (3) base_speed 1.2 to 1.1, a small cut for more correction time, with the oval still well within 3 s; (4) kp 2.0 unchanged, to avoid the jitter seen at kp 2.6; (5) kd 0.6 to 0.8, to damp the faster corrections that the lead creates. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.33 and some slalom completions, s-bend finishes at or above iteration 2 levels, and oval unchanged at about 15-16 finishes. Risks: kd 0.8 could add jitter (oval steering_oscillation was 0.38), and the forward sensors may lose the line on tight bends. Measurements wanted next: slalom progress and max_error to test H5; steering_oscillation to check kd jitter; completion_time on the oval to confirm the time budget; and line_loss_events on the s-bend to see whether the forward sensors lose the line.
